claims.text: Equimolar WTaTiVZr has improved plastic strain relative to commercial pure tungsten at high temperature.
Equimolar WTaTiVZr has improved toughness relative to commercial pure tungsten at high temperature.
Intrinsic lattice distortion is the primary factor governing the alloy's improved plastic strain and toughness.
Lattice distortion in WTaTiVZr enhances the mobility of edge dislocations at high temperature.
Enhanced edge-dislocation mobility reduces brittle failure by enabling more extensive plastic deformation.
WTaTiVZr is an equimolar, multi-principal-element refractory alloy.
The prepared WTaTiVZr alloy forms a chemically homogeneous BCC solid solution.
The prepared WTaTiVZr alloy has a fine-grained microstructure.
Commercially produced pure tungsten typically has a coarser microstructure than the proposed WTaTiVZr alloy.
Commercial pure tungsten has a high ductile-to-brittle transition temperature that restricts its plasma-facing applications.
Testing WTaTiVZr and pure tungsten under identical thermal, mechanical, geometric, strain-rate, and environmental conditions provides a controlled material comparison.
Temperatures at or above 1000 K define the proposed high-temperature validity range for the mechanism.
The relevant structural mediator is lattice distortion accompanied by a modified dislocation-core structure that favors edge-dislocation motion.
The multi-principal-element design creates heterogeneous lattice strains that lower the activation and glide barriers for edge dislocations.
Easier edge-dislocation activation and glide increase plastic deformation and mechanical energy dissipation.
Increased plastic deformation and energy dissipation raise both plastic strain and toughness relative to pure tungsten.
The proposed mechanism is not asserted to apply at room temperature or under substantially different processing or irradiation regimes.
Failure to observe a statistically significant increase in plastic strain or fracture toughness, or failure to observe enhanced edge-dislocation activity, would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The initial-state description specifies fine-grained WTaTiVZr versus typically coarser commercial tungsten, while the intervention and falsification design call for identical processing and similar microstructural uniformity. These are incompatible comparison strategies, and retaining different grain structures would confound composition and lattice distortion with grain-size effects.
